articles.title: The Croman name is back in the deal flow, featuring the next generation
articles.narrative: Jake and Adam Croman, operating independently from their father, have acquired a five-story, half rent-stabilized apartment building at 118 Mulberry Street in Chinatown, New York City. This acquisition reflects their strategy of investing in smaller multifamily buildings with commercial storefronts, a departure from traditional value-add approaches in the current rent-stabilized market. The transaction highlights a generational shift in investment philosophy within the Croman family, focusing on assets that many other investors are currently avoiding.

data_points.address: 118 Mulberry Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Approximately half of the units are rent-stabilized.

articles.title: Alexander brothers swept into contraband probe at Brooklyn detention center
articles.narrative: This article reports on a contraband cellphone probe at a Brooklyn detention center involving the Alexander brothers, formerly prominent residential real estate brokers. Federal prosecutors charged another inmate with possessing an illegal phone, which was allegedly used by Oren Alexander and others. The report also revealed that all three Alexander brothers were found to have used contraband cellphones, though they have not been charged with related crimes. The article also touches on Tal Alexander's divorce proceedings, which revealed communications from him while in detention, and allegations that he orchestrated an early lease termination for the apartment he shared with his estranged wife at 432 Park Avenue.

articles.title: What we learned from Zillow’s courtroom clash with Chicago MLS and Compass
articles.narrative: A federal judge is deliberating a dispute between Zillow, Compass, and Chicago's multiple listing service (MLS), Midwest Real Estate Data (MRED), regarding control over residential real estate listings. Zillow alleges that MRED's decision to cut off its data feed in May was a coordinated boycott to protect Compass's private exclusive listings, which Zillow claims create a 'velvet rope' effect in the market. Compass and MRED, however, assert that Zillow failed to comply with objective criteria rules for listing filtering, with MRED's CEO defending the decision as an enforcement of fair listing practices. The outcome of this case could significantly impact the future of residential inventory control and the traditional MLS ecosystem nationwide.
